audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s, AUD 150K+. Value means quality per dollar at the luxury end, never cheap. The paying parent wants to see where the money goes and that it is protected.

payload.search_intent: Commercial investigation: which luxury destinations give the most for a serious budget, and how to judge that.
payload.angle: The only ranked list with its method on show. Each destination is ranked on what our own cost guides publish (figure as worded, currency, year, guest count), what a luxury budget buys there, and season and lead time, then the invisible costs a Wedded Advisor manages show why the cheapest headline is not the best value.
serp_gaps_to_win: No AU result ranks destinations by luxury value with stated criteria.
No result gives currency, year and guest count for its figures.
No result separates value from cheap for a high-budget couple.
No result explains the hidden costs (room blocks, transfers, VAT, exchange rate, wet weather) that change real value.
Related searches 'best value luxury destination wedding cost' and '... packages' are unserved.

outline.answers: What does best value mean here and how was the list built?
must_include: Value defined as quality per dollar at the luxury end, not the lowest price
Criteria: figures our own cost guides publish, quoted as worded with currency, year and guest count; what a luxury budget buys there; season and lead time where our pages state them
Say plainly that guide figures use different guest counts and currencies, so the ranking is an editorial judgement, not a like-for-like price table
No conversions to AUD; no competitor figures or rankings
Link the cost-by-region article for averages

outline.h2: The best value luxury destination weddings ranked
outline.answers: Which destinations give the most for a luxury budget, in order?
must_include: 6 or 7 H3 cards, each: figure as worded from our guide with a descriptive link, what it buys, best season only if sourced, who it suits

Proposed order (researcher to confirm against live pages): 1 Santorini, Greece (our breakdown: from €4,000 for an elopement to €55,000 or more); 2 Puglia, Italy (our page: better value than Tuscany or Como; quote a figure only if the page gives one); 3 Fiji (our Fiji cost page FJD $10,000 to $30,000, check its conversion note; else use the Fiji destination page with no figure); 4 Dubai (our Dubai cost guide: hotel packages from AED 200 per person, per-person basis stated); 5 Maldives (our breakdown: US$25,000 to US$60,000 all-in for 20 guests); 6 Amalfi Coast (our breakdown: €60,000 to €110,000 or more for 60 to 80 guests); 7 Lake Como (our 2026 to 27 guide: €80,000 to €150,000 for 60 guests over three days; real-weddings breakdown gives €45,000 to €90,000 for 60 guests, researcher to pick one and note the difference)
Italy context line: our Italy guide's €20,000 to over €120,000 range by region, season and guest count
Every figure carries its currency, year or guide date, and guest count

outline.h2: Why Bali sits outside the ranking for now
outline.answers: Where is Bali, a favourite for Australians?
must_include: Mention Bali with NO figures (SITE-CONFLICTS: USD range in the cost guide vs AUD range on the hub)
Link the Bali hub with a non-exact anchor
Say a Wedded Advisor can scope a Bali budget on a call

outline.h2: What makes a luxury wedding good value
outline.answers: How do we judge value beyond the headline price?
must_include: Exclusive use vs shared resort, guest experience across several days, service ratios, what packages include vs exclude
Package vs bespoke trade-off; link /destination-wedding-packages and the all-inclusive cost guide
Bargain hunter guardrail: no 'cheap' framing

outline.h2: The hidden costs that change the ranking
outline.answers: What costs do headline figures leave out?
must_include: Invisible work: guest room blocks and attrition, transfers, wet-weather plan, legal paperwork, VAT or local taxes, planner fees, exchange-rate movement between deposit and final payment
Link hidden costs article and wedding planner cost article
Lake Como guide note: welcome aperitivo and farewell lunch can add 25 to 40% (own page; researcher to confirm)

outline.h2: Season and lead time and how they move the price
outline.answers: When should we marry and how early should we book to get the best value?
must_include: Only seasons our pages state (Greece best-time article, Puglia page best months, others if sourced)
Shoulder season vs peak in general terms; lead time for villas and resorts
No invented month figures

outline.h2: How a Wedded Advisor protects your budget from Australia
outline.answers: How do we plan this well from the other side of the world without hiring the wrong people?
must_include: Couple fear 1: hiring the wrong planner (vetted vendors, no kickbacks framing only if brand-profile supports it)
Couple fear 2: planning from overseas (time zones, slow replies, someone on the ground)
One point of contact for venue, travel, vendors and payments (wording from /wonderland-concierge description)
Paying parent: clear view of where money goes
CTA discovery_call

outline.h2: Best value luxury destination wedding questions answered
must_include: 5 FAQs: Which destination gives the best value for a luxury wedding? How much should we budget for a luxury destination wedding? Are all-inclusive packages good value at the luxury end? When is the best time to book for value? Is a destination wedding cheaper than a wedding at home? (answer by linking the vs-home article, no competitor figures)
FAQ answers reuse only figures already in the body
Couple fear 1, wrong planner: answered in the Wedded Advisor section
Couple fear 2, planning from overseas: answered in the Wedded Advisor section
Transparent ranking method near the top
Every figure quoted as worded from our own guide, with currency, year and guest count, and linked
Bali mentioned without figures
Invisible work section (room blocks, transfers, wet weather, legal, budget, FX)
